title: Counting up to give change
examples: How do I work out change?
What is the change from 100 for 65?
Why count up instead of taking away?

explain.say: You buy a mango for 65 rupees and pay with a 100 rupee note. How much change should you get? Many shopkeepers count up instead of taking away. Look at the number line: from 65 we hop up to 100. That is 35 in all.
First hop to the next ten. From 65, add 5 to reach 70. See the small hop? A little jump to a tidy ten makes it easy. How far is 70 from 100?
Now jump in tens: 80, 90, 100. That is 3 tens, which is 30. So from 70, add 30 to reach 100. Can you add up the two jumps?
5 and 30 make 35. So from 65, you add 35 to reach 100, and your change is 35 rupees. It is the same as 100 take away 65, but much easier! Can you check it by adding 65 and 35?

Brilliant! Try 75 from 100: hop 5 to 80, then 20 more to 100, so the change is 25. Wow: before calculators, shopkeepers everywhere counted change like this. Challenge: what is the change from 50 for 38?

faq.q: How do I work out change?
faq.a: Count up from the price to the money you paid. Hop to the next ten, then jump in tens. From 65 to 100 is 5 and then 30, so the change is 35.

faq.q: What is the change from 100 for 65?
faq.a: The change is 35. From 65, add 5 to make 70, then add 30 to make 100. 5 and 30 make 35.

faq.q: Why count up instead of taking away?
faq.a: Counting up uses small, easy hops to tidy tens, so you avoid regrouping. 100 take away 65 needs borrowing, but counting up does not.
asks: Is counting up easier than subtracting?

faq.q: How can I check my change?
faq.a: Add the change to the price. If you get the money you paid, it is right: 65 plus 35 is 100.
asks: How do I know the change is right?

faq.q: What is the change from 50 for 38?
faq.a: Count up from 38: add 2 to make 40, then 10 to make 50. 2 and 10 make 12, so the change is 12.

facts: Counting up from the price to the amount paid is often called the shopkeeper's method.

quiz.say: You pay 100 for a book costing 80. What is your change?
quiz.show: You pay 100 for a book costing 80. What is your change?

wrong.1: 80 is the price, not the change.
wrong.2: 180 adds the numbers instead of finding the difference.

quiz.say: Counting up from 46 to 100, what is the first hop to a tidy ten?
quiz.show: Counting up from 46 to 100, what is the first hop to a tidy ten?

wrong.0: 46 plus 6 is 52, which is not a tidy ten.
wrong.2: 46 plus 10 is 56, which jumps past the tidy ten.
